## `snowflake` {#connection-snowflake}

A Snowflake account, the user that kayak connects as, and the warehouse that runs the statements. kayak uses the SQL API of Snowflake. The output or the input sets the table.

`warehouse`, `database`, `schema` and `role` go to Snowflake as you write them. Snowflake compares them with case, so write them as `SHOW` lists them. This is usually in upper case.

A statement that kayak runs starts the warehouse if the warehouse is suspended. Thus, a short `interval_secs` on an input or small batches on an output can keep the warehouse running and cost credits all day.

| field | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account` | `string` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | The account identifier, as `orgname-accountname`, for example `myorg-account1`. kayak uses it to find the server and to sign the token. For an account locator, write only the locator (`xy12345`) and write the full address in `url`. |
| `user` | `string` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | The user to connect as. |
| `auth` | `key_pair \| token` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | How kayak signs in. |
| `warehouse` | `string` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | The warehouse that runs the statements. |
| `database` | `string` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | The database to use. The database must exist. The output makes tables. It does not make databases. |
| `schema` | `string` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | The schema to use. The schema must exist. A `table` with a schema (`staging.readings`) replaces this value. |
| `allow_http` | `boolean` | <Badge type="info" text="optional" /> | Permit an `http://` url with no TLS. The default is false. The credentials go with every request, as plain text. Use it only for a local test server. |
| `role` | `string` | <Badge type="info" text="optional" /> | The role to use. The default is the default role of the user. |
| `statement_timeout_seconds` | `integer` | <Badge type="info" text="optional" /> | How long one statement can run before Snowflake cancels it, in seconds. The default is 300. A long statement keeps the warehouse running. |
| `url` | `string` | <Badge type="info" text="optional" /> | The url of the server, when `account` does not give it. Use it for an account locator with a region, for private connectivity or for an account in China. For example, `https://xy12345.us-east-2.aws.snowflakecomputing.com`. |

**`auth` — `type: "key_pair"`**

| field | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `private_key` | `string` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | The private key, as an unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM that starts with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. Use a `${NAME}` secret reference for this value. kayak has no way to open an encrypted key. |

**`auth` — `type: "token"`**

| field | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | `string` | <Badge type="warning" text="required" /> | The token. Use a `${NAME}` secret reference for this value. |
